# Untyped-Evidence Migration Candidates — Triage Scan

**Date:** 2026-08-08
**Generated by:** `scripts/check/scan-untyped-evidence-candidates.shs`
**Design doc:** `doc/05_design/infra/sspec/untyped_evidence_migration_design.md`
**Progress (updated after each batch):** 24 migrated ("yes"), 64 explicitly
rejected ("reject: ..."), of 1119 total category-1 candidate rows. Resume by
pulling the next unmigrated block (rows still marked "no") in file order.

This report enumerates and categorizes every `*_spec.spl` file under
`test/01_unit/` and `test/02_integration/` (excluding the frozen legacy
mirror `test/unit/` and `.spipe_matchers_*` generated shadow files)
against the three categories defined in the design doc. This converts the
previously unbounded "full-repo untyped-evidence migration" plan item into
a finite, reviewable list. **Enumerating this list is the deliverable of
this lane** — migrating any individual item on it is separate, per-item
work, per the design doc's own migration rule (section 4): every
category-1 hit below requires manual confirmation before conversion, this
scan only narrows the search.

## Heuristic limitations

This is a heuristic line-pattern scan, not a perfect classifier:
- It detects co-occurrence of a capture-call pattern and an
  `expect(...).to_contain()/.to_equal()` call within the same `it` block,
  not actual data-flow from the captured value into the assertion.
- Category 3 (print-only) detection is a simple presence check for a bare
  `print`/`println` call with no assertion signal in the same block; it
  does not attempt AST-level scoping.
- `it` blocks are detected by the repo's 4-space-indent `it "..."`/`it(`
  convention; specs using a different indentation or block form are not
  reliably split and may be scored as a single block.
- False positives/negatives are expected. Every category-1 candidate
  listed below still requires a human read of the actual file before any
  migration, exactly as the design doc's migration rule requires.
